messages:
Maria Chen: Heads-up — cutoff in ~6h. We have a couple of incoming changes that need changelog entries and potentially a version bump. I spotted a breaking SDK change in PR #1234 (auth field rename) and a runtime perf tweak in PR #1245. Can owners confirm how we should represent these and whether we need a bump beyond patch?

Ashwin Patel: I can take runtime. PR #1245 is a perf micro-optimization, non-breaking. Patch bump only if we want to be explicit, but no migration notes required.

Jordan Lee: I can own the SDK entry. The auth rename is breaking for some integrations. Recommend a minor bump for the SDK package and a clear migration note.

Maria Chen: Thanks. To be concrete: split the changelog into two entries (SDK and runtime) and bump SDK minor. Runtime stays patch. Also please use the release notes template — short, one-liner + migration note for breaking.

Jordan Lee: Copy. Draft changelog snippet I'll push in a minute. Template I'm using: 

```
- Component: SDK
  PR: #1234
  Type: BREAKING
  Description: Rename `auth_token` -> `auth_header` in SDK config.
  Migration: Update any callers to set the `Authorization` header or update config key.

- Component: Runtime
  PR: #1245
  Type: PATCH
  Description: Small attention-kernel perf optimization (no API change).
```

Olivia Park: @release-bot can you queue the version bump for SDK from 2.1.0 -> 2.2.0 and runtime 1.4.3 -> 1.4.4? We want staging deployment after release cut. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

release-bot: queued: sdk v2.2.0 (pending approval), runtime v1.4.4 (auto). Run `./scripts/release prepare --review` to see diffs.

Ashwin Patel: Fine with those bumps. One small note: please add the component tag `eng-runtime` to the runtime entry so release notes grouping works.

Maria Chen: Good call. Assigning: @Jordan update SDK changelog + open the bump PR; @Ashwin add runtime entry with `eng-runtime` tag. If no objections by +2h I'll merge both.

Jordan Lee: 👍 will send PR in ~30m.

Olivia Park: I'll monitor staging and post a short QA checklist once builds land.

Maria Chen: Thanks all. Quick reminder — use the one-liner style (no long paragraphs) so release notes stay scannable. If you want an example, reuse the format Jordan posted above.
